paper.title: Dysregulation of innate and adaptive serum mediators precedes systemic lupus erythematosus classification and improves prognostic accuracy of autoantibodies

nodes.text: Dysregulation of innate and adaptive serum mediators precedes systemic lupus erythematosus classification and improves prognostic accuracy of autoantibodies
nodes.description: Journal of Autoimmunity 74 (2016) 182-193. Longitudinal study of 84 pre-SLE individuals and 86 matched controls from the Department of Defense Serum Repository measuring autoantibodies and 32 soluble mediators.
nodes.anchor: Dysregulation of innate and adaptive serum mediators precedes systemic lupus erythematosus classification and improves prognostic accuracy of autoantibodies

nodes.text: Longitudinal analysis of serum samples from 84 individuals before SLE classification and 86 matched healthy controls measuring autoantibodies and soluble immune mediators
nodes.description: Samples from the Department of Defense Serum Repository (DoDSR) collected prior to and at/after SLE classification (average 5.98 years pre-classification). Cases had average 2.96 samples, controls average 2 samples. 416 total samples analyzed. Samples divided into four time periods relative to SLE classification for longitudinal analysis.
nodes.anchor: Samples were obtained from the DoDSR. Demographic and clinical information, including medication history and American College of Rheumatology (ACR) criteria for SLE classification, were extracted from medical records by study personnel.

nodes.text: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for BLyS (R&D Systems) and APRIL (eBioscience/Affymetrix) per manufacturer's protocol
nodes.description: Serum levels of BLyS and APRIL assessed using ELISA kits from R&D Systems (Minneapolis, MN) and eBioscience/Affymetrix (San Diego, CA) respectively, following manufacturer protocols.
nodes.anchor: Serum levels of BLyS (R & D Systems, Minneapolis, MN) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) (eBioscience/Affymetrix, San Diego, CA) were assessed using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) per manufacturer's protocol.

nodes.text: xMAP multiplex assays (eBioscience/Affymetrix) for 30 immune mediators including cytokines, chemokines, and soluble TNFR superfamily members
nodes.description: Normalized fluorescence intensity values for 30 immune mediators determined by xMAP multiplex assays. Quality control performed; four mediators (IFN-α, TNF-α, IL-10, IL-15) excluded due to >50% measurements below detection limit. Average inter-assay CV 10.5%, intra-assay CV <10%.
nodes.anchor: Normalized fluorescence intensity values for an additional 30 immune mediators, including cytokines, chemokines, and soluble TNFR superfamily members (Supplemental Table 2), were determined by xMAP multiplex assays (eBioscience/Affymetrix) [18].

nodes.text: BioPlex 2200 system (Bio-Rad Technologies) for simultaneous detection of autoantibody specificities: dsDNA, chromatin, Ro/SSA, La/SSB, Sm, SmRNP, and RNP
nodes.description: Semi-quantitative values for anti-dsDNA reported as IU/mL (positive ≥10 IU/mL). All other autoantibody specificities reported in autoantibody index (AI) units based on fluorescence intensity (range 0-8) using manufacturer-specified positive cutoff (positive ≥1 AI). Factor XIIIb levels evaluated as quality control.
nodes.anchor: The BioPlex 2200® system (Bio-Rad Technologies) was used to simultaneously detect levels of multiple autoantibody specificities within a single serum sample: dsDNA, chromatin, Ro/SSA, La/SSB, Sm, SmRNP, and RNP [7,35].

nodes.text: Mixed linear regression models fitted on normalized FI values of each soluble mediator over time using lme4 package in R (version 2.15.0) with intercepts as random effects and disease status as fixed effect
nodes.description: Used to assess longitudinal changes in soluble mediator levels. Non-parametric rank-based analysis with GraphPad Prism 6.0 for asymmetric distributions. P-values adjusted by false discovery rate (FDR) using fdrtools package. Kaplan-Meier survival curves for timing of dysregulation. Cox proportional hazard models for hazard ratios. Random forest classification with randomForest R package (ntree=2000, mtry=sqrt(p), importance=TRUE, proximity=TRUE). Stepwise variable selection using Genuer and Tuleau-Malot algorithm.

nodes.text: What immune dysregulation beyond autoantibody accumulation contributes to preclinical SLE pathogenesis and transition to clinical disease?
nodes.description: The paper investigates whether soluble mediators from innate and adaptive immune pathways are dysregulated prior to SLE classification and whether they improve prognostic accuracy over autoantibodies alone.
nodes.anchor: To determine if other forms of immune dysregulation contribute to preclinical SLE pathogenesis, we measured SLE-associated autoantibodies and soluble mediators in samples from 84 individuals collected prior to SLE classification

nodes.text: What is the temporal relationship between soluble mediator dysregulation and autoantibody accumulation during preclinical SLE development?
nodes.description: The study compares timing of autoantibody specificity detection and soluble mediator dysregulation as patients approach SLE classification.
nodes.anchor: To better understand the temporal relationship between soluble mediator dysregulation and autoantibody production, we next compared the timing of autoantibody specificity detection and soluble mediator dysregulation as patients moved toward SLE classificat

nodes.text: Multiple soluble mediators including IL-5, IL-6, and IFN-γ are significantly elevated in pre-SLE individuals more than 3.5 years before classification, prior to or concurrent with autoantibody positivity.
nodes.description: In the earliest time period (>3.5 years pre-classification), cases showed elevated IL-6 (q=6.83×10⁻⁶), IL-12p70 (q=0.013), IFN-γ (q=0.035), IL-4 (q=0.01), IL-5 (q=3.6×10⁻⁶), IP-10 (q=0.023), and decreased TGF-β (q=0.023) compared to matched controls.
nodes.anchor: Cases who later developed SLE exhibited increased inflammatory mediators from multiple immune pathways more than 3.5 years pre-classification (Fig. 1 and Table 1).

nodes.text: Innate cytokines, IFN-associated chemokines, and soluble TNF superfamily mediators increase longitudinally in pre-SLE cases approaching classification but not in healthy controls.
nodes.description: Cases gained an average of 0.5 dysregulated mediators per year vs 0.06 in controls (p<0.001). Significant longitudinal increases in IP-10 (p<0.001), MIG (p<0.001), IL-2 (p=0.008), IL-5 (p=0.001), IL-21 (p=0.007), BLyS (p=0.008), APRIL (p=0.013), TNFRI (p<0.001), TNFRII (p<0.001).
nodes.anchor: Cases moving toward SLE classification gained an average of 0.5 dysregulated mediators per year, compared to only 0.06 in controls (p < 0.001; Fig. 2A and Table 2).

nodes.text: BLyS and APRIL levels are comparable in pre-SLE cases and controls until less than 10 months before classification, then increase significantly in cases.
nodes.description: BLyS and APRIL were not significantly different >3.5 years pre-classification (q=0.927 and q=0.672) but became significantly elevated in the period 0.9 years before to 0.1 years after classification (q=0.003 and q=0.019). Mixed models confirmed significant longitudinal increases in cases vs controls (BLyS p=0.008, APRIL p=0.013).
nodes.anchor: Of note, multiple TNF superfamily members, including TNFRI, TNFRII, BLyS, and APRIL, were dysregulated only as patients approached SLE classification (Fig. 1 and Table 1).

nodes.text: Dysregulation of adaptive immune mediators (IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IFN-γ, MIG) precedes autoantibody accumulation in preclinical SLE.
nodes.description: Each of these mediators was elevated in >50% of cases by 2 years pre-classification and 85-95% by 2 years post-classification. Hazard ratios show mediator dysregulation significantly more likely than autoantibody positivity for all tested autoantibodies (anti-dsDNA, anti-chromatin, anti-Ro/SSA, anti-La/SSB, anti-RNP, anti-Sm).
nodes.anchor: The detection of most lupus-associated autoantibody specificities occurred significantly later than the onset of IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IFN-γ, or MIG dysregulation (Fig. 3 and Table 3).

nodes.text: Random forest models incorporating ANA and anti-Ro/SSA positivity with IL-5, IL-6, and MIG levels distinguish future SLE patients with 92% accuracy across the entire pre-classification period, compared to 78% accuracy using ANA positivity alone.
nodes.description: In the combined model spanning all pre-classification time: sensitivity 0.93 (0.87-0.97), specificity 0.89 (0.77-0.96), PPV 0.96 (0.90-0.99), NPV 0.84 (0.71-0.93), accuracy 92% (±1.78%). ANA-only model: accuracy 78% (±2.42%). Soluble mediators alone (IP-10, IL-5, IL-6): accuracy 84% (±2.95%).
nodes.anchor: Over the entire pre-classification period, random forest models incorporating ANA and anti-Ro/SSA positivity with levels of IL-5, IL-6, and the IFN-γ-induced chemokine, MIG, distinguished future SLE patients with 92% (±1.8%) accuracy, compared to 78% accur

nodes.text: A distinct ANA-negative but IL-5/IFN-γ-high pre-SLE cluster is associated with higher risk of nephritis at classification, while ANA-positive cases are more likely to develop arthritis.
nodes.description: SLE cluster 1 (ANA-negative, IL-5 high, IFN-γ high) showed no difference in sex, race, age, or medication history compared to ANA-positive cluster, but had higher nephritis risk (p=0.008). ANA-positive cluster had higher arthritis risk (p=0.028).
nodes.anchor: However, ANA negative, IL-5 and IFN-γ high cases (SLE cluster 1) were more likely to develop nephritis (p = 0.008), while cases who were ANA positive were more likely to develop arthritis (p = 0.028) as they transitioned to classified SLE.

nodes.text: Early dysregulation of Th-type cytokines IL-5 (Th2) and IL-6 (Th2/Th17) may be an essential early step in SLE pathogenesis, contributing to all stages of disease.
nodes.description: IL-5 and IL-6 elevated in ~20% of future SLE patients at least 6 years pre-classification and ~90% by 2 years post-classification. They were independent classifiers in most multivariate random forest models. IL-5 and IL-6 support T cell survival and antibody production, suggesting they promote autoantibody production.
nodes.anchor: Indeed, these two mediators were elevated in about 20% of future SLE patients at least 6 years prior to disease transition and in approximately 90% of SLE patients by two years after classification.

nodes.text: IFN-γ elevation precedes autoantibodies and drives BLyS/APRIL production, supporting a model where simultaneous dysregulation of T helper, regulatory, IFN-related, and TNF-related pathways erodes immune tolerance.
nodes.description: IFN-γ elevated >3.5 years pre-classification. IFN-γ and IFN-α stimulate BLyS/APRIL production. BLyS/APRIL increase significantly within 1 year of classification. ANA positivity did not exclude IFN-γ from multivariate models, suggesting distinct roles.
nodes.anchor: Thus, the early elevation of IFN-γ, followed by significant increases in BLyS and APRIL within one year of disease classification when SLE is imminent, supports the model that simultaneous dysregulation of T helper, regulatory, IFN-related, and TNF-related

nodes.description: From Table 1: median normalized fluorescence intensity values with interquartile ranges for cases (n=61) and controls (n=56) in the earliest time period, with FDR-adjusted q-values.

nodes.text: Cases gained an average of 0.5 dysregulated mediators per year (p<0.001) and 0.3 autoantibody specificities per year (p<0.001), while controls gained 0.06 mediators/year and 0 autoantibody specificities/year.
nodes.description: From mixed linear regression models (Table 2) and Supplemental Fig. 3/Table 2. Cases had mean 12.7 elevated mediators at classification (up from 8.8 >3.5 years prior) vs controls 6.3 (up from 5.7). Cases had mean 3.0 autoantibody specificities at classification (up from 1.0) vs controls consistently 0.1.
nodes.anchor: Cases moving toward SLE classification gained an average of 0.5 dysregulated mediators per year, compared to only 0.06 in controls (p < 0.001; Fig. 2A and Table 2).

nodes.text: BLyS increased significantly in cases (slope 93.93 pg/ml/year) vs controls (18.38 pg/ml/year), p=0.008; APRIL increased in cases (slope 1415 pg/ml/year) vs controls (288 pg/ml/year), p=0.013, with significant differences only in the period <0.9 years before classification.
nodes.description: From Table 2 mixed linear regression slopes and Table 1 q-values. BLyS and APRIL not different >3.5 years pre-classification (q=0.927, q=0.672) but significantly elevated 0.9 years before to 0.1 years after (q=0.003, q=0.019).

nodes.text: Hazard ratios for mediator dysregulation vs autoantibody positivity: IL-5 vs anti-dsDNA 5.28 (3.56-7.82), IL-6 vs anti-dsDNA 4.22 (2.85-6.25), IFN-γ vs anti-dsDNA 3.06 (2.11-4.44), MIG vs anti-dsDNA 4.11 (2.80-6.06); all p<10⁻⁸.
nodes.description: From Table 3: composite ratio of cases with elevated mediator to cases with positive autoantibody at any given time. Hazard ratio >1 indicates mediator more likely positive than autoantibody. Robust log-rank test p-values.

nodes.text: Random forest model across entire pre-classification period: combined predictors (ANA, anti-Ro/SSA, IL-5, IL-6, MIG) achieved 92% accuracy (±1.78%), sensitivity 0.93, specificity 0.89, PPV 0.96, NPV 0.84; ANA-only model 78% accuracy (±2.42%).
nodes.description: From Table 4 'ALL' time period. Ten independent pre-SLE datasets generated with replacement; final model consisted of predictors appearing in at least 5 of 10 best RF models. Average prediction accuracy calculated across the ten datasets.

nodes.text: ANA-negative, IL-5-high, IFN-γ-high pre-SLE cluster (SLE cluster 1) had significantly higher nephritis risk (p=0.008) at classification compared to ANA-positive cluster, which had higher arthritis risk (p=0.028).
nodes.description: From multidimensional scaling of RF proximity matrix (Fig. 4). Clusters compared for sex, race, age, medication history, and individual ACR criteria using Fisher's exact test, chi-square, or unpaired t-test.
nodes.anchor: However, ANA negative, IL-5 and IFN-γ high cases (SLE cluster 1) were more likely to develop nephritis (p = 0.008), while cases who were ANA positive were more likely to develop arthritis (p = 0.028) as they transitioned to classified SLE.

nodes.text: Conduct prospective longitudinal studies of individuals with autoantibody positivity ± immune dysregulation prior to clinical symptoms to determine which autoimmune diseases associate with particular dysregulated immune pathways.
nodes.description: The paper states future prospective studies are needed to determine which autoimmune diseases are associated with particular dysregulated immune pathways present before/concurrent with particular autoantibody specificities or clinical rheumatic disease.

nodes.text: Determine the cellular sources of dysregulated soluble mediators in preclinical SLE.
nodes.description: The discussion explicitly states the cellular sources remain unknown and are the subject of future study.
nodes.anchor: Although the cellular sources of dysregulated soluble mediators in preclinical SLE remain unknown and are the subject of future study

nodes.text: Determine if dysregulation of signaling pathways leading to aberrant cellular activation and secretion of inflammatory mediators is due to genetic, epigenetic, and/or environmental triggers such as vitamin D deficiency or latent EBV infection.
nodes.description: The discussion lists these as additional future studies required.
nodes.anchor: Additional, future studies will be required to determine if dysregulation of signaling pathways that leads to aberrant cellular activation and secretion of inflammatory mediators is due to genetic, epigenetic, and/or environmental triggers
